             blocks writes to it until the copy finishes. [MySQL: blocks writes]
  WARNING    Change column `email`: `varchar(255)` → `varchar(320)`, character set utf8mb3 → utf8mb4. Safe for
             the data. The limit only gets bigger. Sorting, comparisons and unique checks follow the new rules,
             and joins to columns that keep the old collation can no longer use an index. MySQL copies the whole
             table and blocks writes to it until the copy finishes. [MySQL: blocks writes]
  WARNING    Rename column `name` → `full_name`. The data is kept. Treated as a rename because `name` exists only
             in the target, `full_name` only in the source, and both have the same definition. If they are really
             two different columns, replace this CHANGE COLUMN with a DROP COLUMN and an ADD COLUMN. MySQL only
             updates the table definition, so it is instant. [MySQL: instant]

  WARNING    Change column `balance`: `decimal(10,2)` → `decimal(12,2)`. Safe for the data. The new type holds

  WARNING    Change column `state`: `varchar(10)` → `varchar(20)`, NULL allowed → NOT NULL, character set latin1

             (strict mode) if any row holds NULL. Check first: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE state IS NULL`.
             Sorting, comparisons and unique checks follow the new rules, and joins to columns that keep the old
             collation can no longer use an index. MySQL copies the whole table and blocks writes to it until the
             copy finishes. [MySQL: blocks writes]
  WARNING    Change column `ref_code`: `varchar(32)` → `varchar(64)`, character set latin1 → utf8mb4. Safe for
             the data. But MySQL has to copy the table: past 255 bytes, every value needs a 2-byte length field
             instead of 1. Sorting, comparisons and unique checks follow the new rules, and joins to columns that
             keep the old collation can no longer use an index. MySQL copies the whole table and blocks writes to
             it until the copy finishes. [MySQL: blocks writes]
  WARNING    Add column `total_cents` `bigint` after `ref_code`. A STORED generated column: MySQL computes and
             stores it for every existing row. MySQL copies the whole table and blocks writes to it until the
             copy finishes. [MySQL: blocks writes]
  OK         Rename index `customer_id` → `idx_customer`. Same columns; only the name changes. MySQL only updates
             the table definition (no rebuild); reads and writes continue. [MySQL: instant]
  OK         Rename index `idx_ref_old` → `idx_ref`. Same columns; only the name changes. MySQL only updates the

  SUGGESTION Drop foreign key `orders_ibfk_1` (customer_id → `customers`). No data is lost, but MySQL stops
